sentences.nl: In die les leg ik de scheidbare werkwoorden uit.
sentences.en: In that lesson I explain the separable verbs.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• In that lesson explain I the separable verbs out.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "In die les" means "in that lesson," with "die" used as a demonstrative pronoun.  
• "Leg ik ... uit" is a separable verb construction where "uitleggen" (to explain) is split into "leg" and "uit." The base verb "leggen" is conjugated, and "uit" is placed at the end.  
• Separable verbs are common in Dutch; they consist of a verb and a prefix that can be separated in certain tenses.  
• Examples:  
  - "Ik maak de deur open." (I open the door.)  
  - "Hij zet de TV aan." (He turns on the TV.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Tijdens de vergadering bespreken we de nieuwe plannen." (During the meeting, we discuss the new plans.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch language teaching, separable verbs are often highlighted due to their unique behavior in sentences, which can be tricky for learners.

sentences.nl: En ‘uitleggen’ is zelf ook een scheidbaar werkwoord.
sentences.en: And 'uitleggen' is itself also a separable verb.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And 'explain' is itself also a separable verb.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Uitleggen" is a separable verb, which means it can be split into two parts: "uit" (out) and "leggen" (to lay/put). In sentences, these parts can be separated when the verb is conjugated.  
• "Zelf" emphasizes that the subject itself possesses a characteristic.  
• Examples:  
  - "Hij legt het uit." (He explains it.)  
  - "Zij geeft zelf les." (She teaches herself.)  
  - "We moeten het werk zelf doen." (We have to do the work ourselves.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "‘Afwassen’ is ook een scheidbaar werkwoord." (To wash up is also a separable verb.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch, understanding separable verbs is important as they are common in everyday language and can change the meaning of sentences significantly.

sentences.nl: Ik leg het uit.
sentences.en: I explain it.

sentences.nl: Zie je dat? — Het voorvoegsel ‘uit’ komt aan het einde van de zin.
sentences.en: Do you see that? — The prefix 'uit' comes at the end of the sentence.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• See you that? — The prefix 'uit' comes at the end of the sentence.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Zie je dat?" is a question structure where the verb "zie" (see) comes first, followed by the subject "je" (you), and then "dat" (that), typical in Dutch interrogative sentences.  
• "Het voorvoegsel ‘uit’ komt aan het einde van de zin" shows how separable verbs work in Dutch. The prefix "uit-" separates from the main verb and appears at the end of the sentence.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Hij maakt de deur open." (He opens the door.)  
  - "Ze belt haar moeder op." (She calls her mother.)  
  - "Ik schrijf de brief af." (I finish the letter.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Kom je morgen langs?" (Are you coming by tomorrow?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Separable verbs are a common feature in Dutch and can often change the meaning of the base verb significantly. Understanding this concept is crucial for mastering Dutch sentence structure.

sentences.nl: De studenten vertellen over zichzelf.
sentences.en: The students talk about themselves.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The students tell about themselves.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De studenten" is the subject of the sentence, meaning "the students."  
• "Vertellen" is the verb, meaning "to tell" or "to talk." It is in the present tense.  
• "Over" is a preposition meaning "about." It is used here to indicate the topic of discussion.  
• "Zichzelf" is a reflexive pronoun meaning "themselves." It is used because the action of telling is directed back to the subject.

• Extra Phrases/Sentences:  
  - "Hij vertelt over zijn reis." (He talks about his trip.)  
  - "Wij praten over het weer." (We talk about the weather.)  
  - "Ze denkt na over haar toekomst." (She thinks about her future.)

## 3. Create a New Example

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• [No cultural note applicable.]

sentences.nl: Ze beantwoorden de vragen van Marieke.
sentences.en: They answer Marieke's questions.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• They answer the questions of Marieke.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ze" is a pronoun meaning "they."  
• "Beantwoorden" is a verb meaning "to answer." In Dutch, verbs are conjugated based on the subject.  
• "De vragen" means "the questions," where "de" is the definite article for plural nouns.  
• "Van" is a preposition meaning "of."  
• "Marieke" is a proper noun, a person's name, which the questions belong to.

Extra phrases/sentences:  
• "Ze lezen de boeken van de bibliotheek." (They read the books of the library.)  
• "Hij beantwoordt de e-mails van zijn baas." (He answers the emails of his boss.)  
• "Wij beantwoorden de brieven van onze vrienden." (We answer the letters of our friends.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zij bekijken de foto's van de vakantie." (They look at the photos of the vacation.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)

sentences.nl: Wie ben je? — Waar kom je vandaan? — Welke talen spreek je? — Waarom leer je Nederlands? — Wat is je hobby? — Gianluca zegt: ‘Mijn hobby is uitgaan’.
sentences.en: Who are you? — Where are you from? — What languages do you speak? — Why are you learning Dutch? — What is your hobby? — Gianluca says: ‘My hobby is going out’.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Who are you? — Where come you from? — Which languages speak you? — Why learn you Dutch? — What is your hobby? — Gianluca says: 'My hobby is going out'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Word Order**: The questions use the inverted word order typical of Dutch questions, where the verb comes before the subject (e.g., "Wie ben je?" - "Who are you?").  
• **Question Words**: "Wie" (who), "Waar" (where), "Welke" (which), "Waarom" (why), "Wat" (what) are all question words used to gather information.  
• **Possessive Pronoun**: "Je" is an informal possessive pronoun meaning "your".  
• **Verb Use**: "Zegt" is the third person singular of "zeggen" (to say). "Is" is the third person singular of "zijn" (to be), and "uitgaan" is an infinitive meaning "to go out".

Extra examples:  
• "Waar werk je?" (Where do you work?)  
• "Welke muziek vind je leuk?" (Which music do you like?)  
• "Waarom ben je laat?" (Why are you late?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Wat doe je in je vrije tijd?" (What do you do in your free time?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, asking someone about their hobbies and interests is a common way to start a conversation and show interest in someone's life.

sentences.nl: En van Drentse boerenmeisjes kun je veel leren! hmm…
sentences.en: And you can learn a lot from Drenthe farmer girls! hmm…
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And from Drenthe farmer girls can you much learn!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses inversion, which is common in Dutch when you start with an adverbial phrase ("van Drentse boerenmeisjes"). The verb "kun" (can) comes before the subject "je" (you).  
• "Veel leren" means "to learn a lot." "Veel" is an adverb meaning "much" or "a lot."  
• Example 1: "Van fouten kun je veel leren." (You can learn a lot from mistakes.)  
• Example 2: "In de ochtend drink ik altijd koffie." (In the morning, I always drink coffee.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Uit boeken kun je veel wijsheid halen." (From books, you can gain a lot of wisdom.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Drenthe is a province in the Netherlands known for its rural landscapes and traditional farming. The mention of "Drentse boerenmeisjes" could evoke imagery of traditional Dutch country life.

sentences.nl: Gianluca fluistert tegen Pablo: ‘ik neem jou wel mee’.
sentences.en: Gianluca whispers to Pablo: 'I'll take you with me'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Gianluca whispers to Pablo: 'I take you indeed with'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Word Order**: The sentence follows a typical Dutch structure where the verb comes early in the main clause ("fluistert"). In the subordinate clause ('ik neem jou wel mee'), the subject-verb-object order is used.  
• **Verb Tense**: "Neem" is the present tense of "nemen" (to take), indicating an action happening now.  
• **Preposition Use**: "Tegen" is used with verbs like "fluisteren" (to whisper) to indicate the person being whispered to.  
• **Particle "wel"**: It can add emphasis or assurance, often translated as 'indeed' or 'certainly' in this context.

Examples:  
• Hij fluistert tegen zijn zus: ‘Ik kom zo terug’. (He whispers to his sister: 'I'll be right back'.)  
• Zij neemt haar hond wel mee naar het park. (She indeed takes her dog to the park.)  
• Wij praten tegen de leraar na de les. (We talk to the teacher after class.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Lisa zegt tegen haar vriend: 'Ik help jou wel met je huiswerk'. (Lisa says to her friend: 'I will indeed help you with your homework'.)

sentences.nl: Beste studenten, we gaan een oefening maken.
sentences.en: Dear students, we are going to do an exercise.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Best students, we go an exercise make.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Beste studenten" is a form of address or greeting. "Beste" is often used in letters or speeches to address a group politely.  
• "We gaan" uses the present tense of "gaan" (to go), which is often used to indicate a future action, similar to "going to" in English.  
• "Een oefening maken" literally translates to "make an exercise," which is a common Dutch way to talk about doing exercises or activities.

Extra examples:  
• "Beste collega's, we beginnen met de vergadering." (Dear colleagues, we are starting the meeting.)  
• "We gaan een boek lezen." (We are going to read a book.)  
• "Ik ga een taart bakken." (I am going to bake a cake.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Beste vrienden, we gaan een wandeling maken." (Dear friends, we are going to take a walk.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• None

sentences.nl: Je mag niet afkijken.
sentences.en: You are not allowed to peek.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• You may not look off.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Je mag niet afkijken" uses the modal verb "mag" (may) in combination with the infinitive "afkijken" (to look off/cheat). The structure is: [subject] + [modal verb] + [negative] + [infinitive verb].  
• "Afkijken" is a separable verb, where "af" is the prefix that can be separated in some tenses.  
• Example: "Je mag hier niet roken." (You may not smoke here.)  
• Example: "Hij mag morgen blijven." (He may stay tomorrow.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Je mag niet te laat komen. (You may not arrive late.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch schools, the phrase "niet afkijken" is commonly used during exams or tests to remind students not to cheat by looking at someone else's work.

sentences.nl: Ben je klaar, dan moet je de oefening bij mij inleveren.
sentences.en: Are you ready, then you must submit the exercise to me.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Are you ready, then must you the exercise with me hand in.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses an inversion structure in "Ben je klaar," where the verb "Ben" (are) comes before the subject "je" (you) due to the question form.  
• "Dan moet je" uses a modal verb "moet" (must), which indicates obligation. The verb "moet" comes second in the clause, following the word order rule for main clauses.  
• "Inleveren" is a separable verb, and in this context, it means "hand in." The prefix "in-" is separated and placed at the end of the clause.  
• Example 1: "Als je klaar bent, kun je het boek teruggeven." (If you are ready, you can return the book.)  
• Example 2: "Moet ik het formulier nu invullen?" (Must I fill in the form now?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Zodra je de toets hebt gemaakt, moet je hem inleveren bij de docent. (As soon as you have completed the test, you must hand it in to the teacher.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch schools and universities, it's common for students to hand in assignments or exercises directly to the teacher, either in person or through a designated submission method. This sentence reflects that practice of direct interaction.

sentences.nl: Dan zal ik het nakijken.
sentences.en: Then I will check it.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Then will I it check.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses future tense with "zal" (will), indicating a future action.  
• The word order is subject-verb-object, but "dan" (then) is placed at the beginning for emphasis or sequence.  
• "Nakijken" is a separable verb, meaning "to check" or "to review," and is split here around the pronoun "het" (it).

• Example 1: Morgen zal hij de auto wassen. (Tomorrow he will wash the car.)  
• Example 2: Eerst zal ik de tafel dekken. (First, I will set the table.)  
• Example 3: Dan zullen we samen werken. (Then we will work together.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Dan zal ik de deur sluiten. (Then I will close the door.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, planning and punctuality are valued. Using "dan" at the beginning of a sentence often helps to clarify the sequence of planned actions, reflecting a cultural preference for orderliness and structure.

sentences.nl: Marieke deelt de oefening uit.

sentences.nl: De studenten vullen de antwoorden in.
sentences.en: The students fill in the answers.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The students fill the answers in.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Vullen ... in" is a separable verb in Dutch, meaning "to fill in." The separable prefix "in" moves to the end of the sentence in the present tense.  
• "De studenten" is the subject, meaning "the students."  
• "De antwoorden" is the plural form of "het antwoord" (the answer), and it serves as the direct object.  

Extra phrases:  
• "Hij vult het formulier in." (He fills in the form.)  
• "Wij vullen de gegevens in." (We fill in the data.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Forms and paperwork are common in Dutch education and bureaucracy, so the phrase "vullen ... in" is frequently used in everyday life.

sentences.nl: Oew… wat ben je streng Marieke…
sentences.en: Ooh... how strict you are, Marieke...

## 1. Literal Translation  
• Oew… what are you strict Marieke…

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence begins with an interjection "Oew," expressing surprise or emphasis.  
• "Wat ben je streng" is an informal way to express that someone is being strict. "Wat" is used here as an exclamatory form meaning "how" rather than "what."  
• The word order "wat ben je" (how are you) is used for emphasis in exclamatory sentences.

Extra examples:  
• Wat ben je snel! (How fast you are!)  
• Wat is het koud vandaag! (How cold it is today!)

sentences.nl: Ze staat op, en ze levert de oefening in.
sentences.en: She gets up, and she submits the exercise.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• She stands up, and she submits the exercise in.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Staat op" is a separable verb meaning "to stand up." In Dutch, separable verbs often split, with the prefix moving to the end of the clause.  
• "Levert in" is another separable verb, meaning "to submit." Like "staat op," the prefix "in" is separated in the sentence.  
• The sentence uses a simple present tense, which is common for describing current actions.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Hij maakt het huiswerk af." (He finishes the homework.)  
  - "Zij trekt haar jas aan." (She puts on her coat.)  
  - "Ik schrijf het rapport op." (I write down the report.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hij staat op, en hij neemt een besluit. (He stands up, and he makes a decision.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No culture note.

sentences.nl: ‘Wat moet ik doen?’ vraagt ze aan Marieke.
sentences.en: "What should I do?" she asks Marieke.

sentences.nl: Rust jij maar even uit.
sentences.en: You just take a rest.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Rest you just for a moment out.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Rust jij maar even uit" uses the imperative mood with "rust" as the verb. "Maar" here softens the command, making it more of a suggestion or encouragement. "Even" means "for a moment" or "a bit", adding a sense of brevity. "Uit" is a separable prefix that means "out", making "uitrusten" (to rest) a separable verb.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Pak jij maar even een stoel." (Just grab a chair for a moment.)  
  - "Kijk maar even rond." (Just have a look around.)  
  - "Luister maar even goed." (Just listen carefully for a moment.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Neem jij maar even pauze." (Just take a break for a moment.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, using "maar" in commands is common as it makes them sound more polite and less forceful, which aligns with the Dutch preference for direct yet courteous communication.

sentences.nl: Ook de andere studenten, leveren één voor één hun oefening in.
sentences.en: The other students also submit their exercises one by one.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Also the other students, submit one by one their exercise in.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ook" is used to mean "also," indicating addition.  
• The comma after "studenten" is stylistic, emphasizing the action in parts.  
• "Één voor één" means "one by one," a common phrase to indicate sequence.  
• "Inleveren" is a separable verb where "in" comes after the object.

Extra phrases:  
• "Hij levert zijn huiswerk in." (He submits his homework.)  
• "Één voor één kwamen ze binnen." (One by one, they came in.)  
• "De kinderen spelen ook buiten." (The children also play outside.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De leerlingen geven één voor één hun boeken terug. (The students return their books one by one.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch education, turning in exercises ("inleveren") is typically done in a structured manner, often emphasizing orderliness and discipline.

sentences.nl: Je kunt ook een niveau lager…

sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• You can also a level lower…

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Je kunt" is a modal verb structure meaning "you can," where "kunt" is the present tense of "kunnen" (to be able to).  
• "Ook" means "also," indicating an additional option or possibility.  
• "Een niveau lager" means "a level lower," where "niveau" is "level" and "lager" is "lower," indicating a comparative structure.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Je kunt ook een andere route nemen." (You can also take another route.)  
  - "Hij wil een niveau hoger spelen." (He wants to play a level higher.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Je kunt ook een stap terug doen." (You can also take a step back.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch education and workplaces, there are often discussions about levels, such as language proficiency or job positions, and moving "een niveau lager" might imply adjusting expectations or responsibilities.

sentences.en: … with another teacher.

sentences.nl: Of ga je het perfectum leren, van een Drents boerenmeisje? — Eh… misschien kunnen wij vanavond afspreken? — Nee, ik spreek niet met jou af.
sentences.en: Or are you going to learn the perfect tense from a Drenthe farm girl? — Uh... maybe we can meet up tonight? — No, I'm not meeting up with you.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Or are you going to learn the perfect tense, from a Drenthe farm girl? — Eh… maybe we can meet tonight? — No, I do not meet with you.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence begins with "Of" (Or), often used to introduce an alternative or question.  
• "ga je het perfectum leren" uses the present tense of "gaan" (to go) + infinitive ("leren," to learn) to indicate future intention.  
• "afspreken" is a separable verb; "af" separates from "spreken" here as "af" in "afspreken" (to meet/agree on).  
• "Nee, ik spreek niet met jou af" follows the Subject-Verb-Object order, common in Dutch main clauses.

• Examples:  
  - "Ga je straks boodschappen doen?" (Are you going to do groceries later?)  
  - "We spreken morgen om vijf uur af." (We will meet tomorrow at five o'clock.)  
  - "Zij gaat een boek lezen." (She is going to read a book.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Of ga je morgen met mij naar de stad?" (Or are you going to the city with me tomorrow?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Drenthe is a province in the Netherlands known for its rural landscape and history, which might be why a "Drents boerenmeisje" (Drenthe farm girl) is mentioned here.

sentences.nl: Ik geef je extra huiswerk.
sentences.en: I am giving you extra homework.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I give you extra homework.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verb "geef" is the first person singular form of "geven" (to give), indicating present tense.  
• "Je" is an informal pronoun for "you," used as the indirect object.  
• "Extra" is an adjective that means "extra" or "additional," used here to modify "huiswerk" (homework).  
• Dutch word order typically places the verb second, with the subject first and objects after the verb.

Examples:  
• Ik geef je een cadeau. (I give you a gift.)  
• Ze geeft hem een boek. (She gives him a book.)  
• We geven jullie de sleutels. (We give you the keys.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hij geeft haar een compliment. (He gives her a compliment.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, education is highly valued, and giving extra homework might be seen as a way for teachers to help students improve their skills or understanding of a subject.

sentences.en: Can I then stay in your group? — Well...
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• May I then well in your group stay? — Uh...

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Mag ik" is a polite way to ask for permission, using the modal verb "mogen" in present tense.  
• "Dan wel" is used to indicate a condition or concession, often translating to "then" or "in that case."  
• "In jouw groep" uses the preposition "in" followed by the possessive pronoun "jouw."  
• "Blijven" is the infinitive form of the verb "to stay," positioned at the end due to the modal verb construction.

• Extra Examples:  
  - "Mag ik jouw boek lenen?" (May I borrow your book?)  
  - "Kunnen we dan wel naar het park gaan?" (Can we then go to the park?)  
  - "Blijf je in de stad wonen?" (Are you staying in the city?)
